pairs.subject: usage-analytics
pairs.evidence: src/components/modules/evaluator/WeeklyDigestView/ModuleLeaderboard.tsx:12 The per-module usage reports are built only from modules that emitted sessions. A module nobody worked in drops out of the report instead of showing as an explicit zero, so 'unused' looks the same as 'unmeasured'.

techniques.evidence: src/components/modules/evaluator/WeeklyDigestView/ModuleLeaderboard.tsx:12 The leaderboard lists the top 8 of the modules that emitted. moduleActivity is built in src/lib/weekly-digest.ts:56 from the emitted rows only; MODULE_LABELS is imported but used only for labels, never as the frame. SessionAnalyticsDashboard's 'Modules Active' card (index.tsx:95) and the 'Module Performance' list also count only modules with sessions. The time axis is zero-filled (day keys, months) but the module axis is not, which is the 'an exhaustiveness check closes only the axis it encodes' trap.

src/components/modules/evaluator/SessionAnalyticsDashboard/ModuleStatsRow.tsx:100 Rates are measured from completed outcomes (a CLI task succeeding or failing), not from visits. Each percentage is shown next to its own count: the with/without-context success rates carry their sample sizes in parentheses, and each module row shows its session total (line 63).

src/components/modules/evaluator/SessionAnalyticsDashboard/RecentSessionRow.tsx:22 Records do carry free-form prompt text, but the insight is computed and shown only on the user's own machine. A search of these files found no fetch, sendBeacon or keepalive egress; the only network calls go to the app's own local API through relative URLs. This is the golden path's local-first option, so no payload leaves the device.
